explanation: First record rows and columns containing original zeros. Then clear their cells in a second pass, so newly written zeros do not create additional attacks.
timeComplexity: O(r · c). A constant number of row/column or full-matrix scans visits O(r·c) cells.
spaceComplexity: O(r + c) for the row and column sets. Set variants store r+c markers; first-row/column variants keep only two boolean flags.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The first pass records exactly the row and column indices containing an original zero. The second pass changes a cell if and only if one of those recorded indices applies. Since the marker sets are not changed during this pass, newly created zeros cannot trigger additional clearing.
walkthrough: For [[5,0,7],[8,9,2]], the original zero records row 0 and column 1. Clear that full row and that column, giving [[0,0,0],[8,0,2]]. The new zeros do not clear row 1.
edgeCases: A matrix with no zeros is unchanged.
A zero in the first row or column is treated normally.
Multiple zeros may mark overlapping rows or columns.
Rows are modified in place rather than replaced.
